yt.title: 100% in practice, 52% in the exam
notes: On a yes/no test, 50% is pure guessing

lines.text: A hundred percent in practice. [1] Then, the real exam... [2] fifty-two percent. On a yes-or-no test, that's barely better than guessing. [3] What went wrong?
It's like a student who [1] memorises the answer key. [2] A perfect score on the practice paper. [3] But change the questions a little... [4] and they're lost. In AI, this is called overfitting.

yt.title: Overfit, underfit, just right
notes: Overfit: follows every dot, even the noise
Underfit: too simple, low scores even in practice
Just right: follows the real trend

lines.text: Picture it as dots on a graph. [1] Too complex: a wiggly line through every dot, even the random mistakes. That's overfitting. [2] Too simple: a straight line that misses the pattern. That's underfitting: low scores, even in practice. [3] Just right: a smooth curve that follows the real trend.

yt.title: Watch two scores
notes: Stop when the validation score starts falling (early stopping)

lines.text: So how do you catch it? [1] Watch two scores while it trains. [2] The practice score keeps climbing. [3] But the validation score, on data it has never seen, peaks... and starts to fall. [4] The moment it falls, stop training.
The fixes. For overfitting: [1] more data, with more variety. [2] A simpler model. [3] Or stop training early. [4] For underfitting, do the opposite: a bigger model, and train longer.
